correctness.rationale: Higashine’s exhaustive classification fixes three parameterized families. Uniqueness of the point meeting infinitely many lines and of the plane containing more than three lines forces preservation of P and H. At least 16 dual-conic points force preservation of their conic; the missing K-rational conic point forces an affine K-parameter action. Comparing coefficients on the infinite B_c family forces the remaining matrix entries. The resulting action preserves precisely the claimed lines and labeled subfamily. Additive L_q surjectivity yields the whole two-parameter orbit; coefficients of y^q and the constant show distinct embedded subsets. Finite checks in two fields confirm but do not prove the infinite result.

value.rationale: The recent exhaustive Galois-line classification motivates the natural reconstruction question whether projection centers (even together with each deck-group type) determine the ambient curve. Here the complete line-data stabilizer has a connected Ga² whereas the source curve has finite automorphism group, producing a concrete two-parameter family of distinct embedded curves sharing exactly all labelled Galois lines. Both the sharp norm-one boundary for preserving labels and the positive-dimensional reconstruction gap are structural, not routine counts.
